docs.title: Guessing Game
docs.text: This code is a simple guessing game where the user tries to guess a random number between 1 and 10. The game will end once the user correctly guesses the number or has exhausted all attempts.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
The following functions are used in this code:

  • random.randint(1, 10): This function is used to generate a random integer between 1 and 10 inclusive. The return value is stored in the variable secret_number.
  • input: This function is used to get input from the user. In this case, it is used to ask the user to guess the number. The input is then converted to an integer using the int constructor.
  • print: This function is used to print messages to the console. In this case, it is used to display the result of the user's guess.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
The following arguments are used in this code:

  • secret_number: This variable stores the randomly generated number between 1 and 10.
  • guess: This variable stores the user's guess of the number.

docs.title: Return types
docs.text: The return type of this code is a string that indicates whether the user correctly guessed the number or not. If the user correctly guesses the number, it will print "You guessed it right!". Otherwise, it will print "Oops! The correct number was {secret_number}."

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
Here is an example usage of this code:

>>> secret_number = random.randint(1, 10)
>>> guess = int(input("Guess a number between 1 and 10: "))
>>> if guess == secret_number:
...     print("You guessed it right!")
... else:
...     print(f"Oops! The correct number was {secret_number}.")

docs.title: Python Program to Check Even or Odd
docs.text: This program asks the user for a number and checks if it is even or odd. The program uses the modulo operator (%) to determine whether the number is even or odd. If the number is even, it prints "The number is even." Otherwise, it prints "The number is odd."

docs.text:
Here is an example of how the user might use this program:

Enter a number: 42
The number is even.

Or, if the user enters an odd number:

Enter a number: 37
The number is odd.

Note that the input() function is used to prompt the user for input and retrieve it as a string. The int() function is then called on this string to convert it to an integer before using it in the modulo operator.
